models_evaluated: four previously published state-of-the-art dermatology AI models (unnamed in abstract)

links.outcome: Performance of published dermatology AI models on new prospectively collected dataset versus published metrics
links.effect: Performance reduction across all four SOTA models compared to previously published performance metrics, indicating generalizability challenges.
links.quote: When evaluating SOTA models using the MIDAS dataset, we observed performance reduction across all models compared to their previously published performance metrics, indicating challenges to generalizability of current SOTA algorithms.

links.outcome: Model-to-clinician diagnostic performance comparison for malignant vs benign
links.effect: Dermatologists were 79% accurate with top-1 diagnosis differentiating malignant from benign; used as comparative baseline for the models.
links.quote: As a comparative baseline, the dermatologists performing biopsies were 79% accurate with their top-1 diagnosis at differentiating a malignant from benign lesion.

unlisted_practices: Publicly released multimodal benchmark dataset with prospectively collected, paired dermoscopic and clinical images for external testing
Evaluating AI performance by image acquisition distance (15 cm vs 30 cm) and image modality

screen.reason: The study develops and releases a benchmark dataset (MIDAS) and evaluates the external generalization of existing state-of-the-art skin lesion diagnostic algorithms across multimodal and multi-distance images, comparing them against clinician accuracy.
